Triage — first-touch grading (triage seat, session `session_01KTguWpd7WNGYTGmSNY31RL`): promoted to `pm:queue`, type Task. Auto-adjudicated (veto window open in the round report; maintainer may overrule).

Adjudication — **turn it on**: `linterOptions: { reportUnusedDisableDirectives: 'error' }` at the top level of `eslint.config.js`, with the card's own reverse verification (an injected stale disable must turn lint red by name). Why this clears the seat bar: the manual floor pins gate **weakening** (AI has a structural incentive to make CI green); this is the opposite direction — a ratchet close whose false-positive surface is measured (count 0 after #4833/PR #4849, per-rule reconciliation on record), whose recurrence is measured (49 stale directives accumulated, plus the #4850 class that is invisible without it), and whose red condition names the offending line. The `--max-warnings` threshold question the body mentions is explicitly **not** bundled — that is a separate, larger policy with an unmeasured red set.

Dev preconditions (fork, don't force): re-run the stale-directive count on the current ref first — it must still be 0 (in-flight PRs may have added one since the cleanup); if non-zero, fix or report before flipping. Timing note from the card stands: land in a quiet window, since any in-flight PR whose diff obsoletes an existing directive goes red at the moment of the flip.

## PM note — ruled and ready, ⛔ **deliberately NOT dispatched right now: this is not a quiet window.**

Recorded by the `domain:devx` @ objectui execution seat (#5748), PM session `session_019b5UBNMtTzKbVtZZGvFuxe`. ⛔ Not claiming it; recording why it is being passed over so the next round does not read the skip as an oversight.

### The ruling is triage's and I am not touching it

Turn it on — `linterOptions: { reportUnusedDisableDirectives: 'error' }` at the top level of `eslint.config.js`, with the card's own reverse verification. The adjudication is sound: this is a ratchet **close**, the opposite direction from the gate-weakening the manual floor guards against, its false-positive surface is measured at 0, its recurrence is measured at 49, and its red condition names the offending line.

### ⛔ Why it waits: the timing constraint is part of the ruling, not a footnote

Both the card and triage say the same thing:

> any in-flight PR whose diff obsoletes an existing directive goes red **at the moment of the flip** (#4835 was exactly this shape, four of them at once)

**This seat currently has four PRs in flight or queued** — #6189, #6199, #6200, and the folded #5483 + #5439, the last of which touches ~20 `vite.config.ts` files. Flipping a repo-wide lint gate to `error` while that is outstanding is precisely the collision the constraint exists to avoid, and it would land the breakage on **other people's** PRs as well as mine.

⚠️ The blast radius is not zero-by-inspection either. "Does this diff make an existing `eslint-disable` stale?" is not answerable by looking at a diff — it depends on whether the rule still fires at that line after the change, which is why the flip is measured rather than reasoned about.

⭐ Taking it now for throughput would be trading a measured risk to other contributors for one card's worth of progress. The queue drains continuously in this lane; the window will come.

### Dispatch conditions for whoever takes it — all three must hold

1. **This seat's queue is empty or near it**, and ideally the repo's is too.
2. **Re-run the stale-directive count on the current ref first — it must still be 0.** Triage's precondition, and the count is from #4833/PR #4849 on 2026-08-16; nine days and a great many merges have passed. ⛔ If non-zero, fix or report before flipping — do not flip and clean up after.
3. ⛔ **Do not bundle the `--max-warnings` threshold question.** Triage explicitly excluded it as a separate, larger policy with an unmeasured red set, and the card's body raises it only as an open question.

Staying `pm:queue`, unassigned. ⛔ No label change — this note is scheduling, not state.

## Re-checked at 03:24Z — ⛔ still not the window, and the reason has shifted

By the `domain:devx` @ objectui execution seat (#5748), PM session `session_019b5UBNMtTzKbVtZZGvFuxe`. Second scheduled re-check; recording it so the skip stays a decision rather than an oversight, and so the next seat does not re-derive it.

### The seat-local half of condition 1 is now satisfied

My earlier note held this card because **this seat** had four PRs in flight. That is no longer the blocker — tonight's batch has drained: #6204, #6205, #6210, #6215, #6216, #6217, #6218, #6220, #6227, #6228, #6229 all merged, with #6212 and #6232 the only two of mine still open.

### ⛔ The repo-wide half is not, and it is the half that matters

The dispatch condition reads *"this seat's queue is empty or near it, **and ideally the repo's** is too."* Measured just now: **13 open PRs repo-wide**, across several seats, including live code work that is nothing to do with this lane —

- **#6234** — retiring the `direction` sort spelling from a published surface (draft)
- **#6233** — gantt export filename locale-map fix
- **#6082** — layout guide corrections
- plus three dependabot bumps, a release PR, and four governed-surface drafts

⚠️ **The blast radius of this flip lands on other people's PRs, not mine.** Any of those thirteen whose diff happens to make an existing `eslint-disable` redundant goes red **at the moment of the flip**, on a branch whose author did nothing wrong and has no idea this card exists. #4835 is that shape on record — four at once.

And it is not answerable by inspection: "does this diff make a disable stale?" depends on whether the rule still fires at that line *after* the change, which is why the card's own precondition is a measurement rather than a review.

⭐ My seat draining does not make the repo quiet, and reading condition 1 as satisfied because *my* board cleared would be reading the constraint as being about my convenience rather than about other contributors. It is the second.

### Unchanged, and still all three required

1. Repo-wide in-flight work low — **not met**, 13 open.
2. **Re-run the stale-directive count on the current ref; it must be 0** before flipping. The 2026-08-16 measurement from #4833 / PR #4849 is now nine days and several hundred merges old.
3. ⛔ Do not bundle the `--max-warnings` threshold — triage excluded it as a separate policy with an unmeasured red set.

Staying `pm:queue`, unassigned. ⛔ No label change — this is scheduling, not state.

## Re-checked at 04:22Z — ⛔ still held. My board is now empty and it still does not open.

Third scheduled re-check, by the `domain:devx` @ objectui execution seat (#5748), PM session `session_019b5UBNMtTzKbVtZZGvFuxe`.

### This seat is fully drained

#6212 and #6242 merged. **Zero open PRs from this seat, zero devs in flight.** Fourteen landed tonight. So the seat-local reading of condition 1 is unambiguously satisfied — and that is precisely why this re-check is worth recording rather than skipping.

### ⛔ The repo is not quiet, and it re-filled while my queue drained

| | 03:24Z | 04:22Z |
|---|---|---|
| open PRs repo-wide | 13 | **12** |
| of them, live code work from other seats | 3 | **5** |

The count barely moved, and the composition got *worse* for this card. Three PRs that did not exist an hour ago are all touching published source:

- **#6248** — correcting invented keys in live `SchemaExample` fixtures (draft)
- **#6244** — forwarding `RadioGroupSchema.orientation` to the rendered radio group
- **#6239** — delivering `FormSection.visibleWhen` in all four form layouts

plus #6082 and the four governed drafts, two dependabot bumps and the release PR.

⚠️ Flipping `reportUnusedDisableDirectives` to **error** reds any branch whose diff happens to make an existing `eslint-disable` redundant — and #6244 and #6239 are exactly the shape that does it, changing whether a rule fires at a line that currently carries a disable. The authors did nothing wrong and have no idea this card exists. #4835 is that failure on record, four at once.

⭐ The lesson from this round is the one worth leaving here: **an empty queue on this seat is not evidence the repo is quiet.** Mine drained by fourteen merges while the repo's stayed flat, because other seats were filling it at the same rate. Reading condition 1 off my own board would have flipped this an hour ago, into a busier repo than the one I first declined to flip it in.

### Unchanged, all three still required

1. Repo-wide in-flight work low — **not met**, 12 open, 5 of them live code.
2. **Re-run the stale-directive count on the current ref; it must be 0.** The 2026-08-16 measurement is now nine days and several hundred merges stale.
3. ⛔ Do not bundle the `--max-warnings` threshold — separate policy, unmeasured red set.

Staying `pm:queue`, unassigned, ⛔ no label change.

## ⛔ Correcting my own three hold notes: the binding constraint is not "wait for a quiet repo"

By the `domain:devx` @ objectui execution seat, PM session `session_019b5UBNMtTzKbVtZZGvFuxe`. This supersedes the framing in my 01:00Z, 03:24Z and 04:22Z comments — **their conclusion (hold) was right; my stated reason was incomplete, and incomplete in a way that could mislead the next seat.**

### What I got wrong

I have three times written that this card is gated on the repo being quiet, and told the next check-in to re-measure the open-PR count and reconsider when it drops. Re-reading the card's own words:

> 当前该类在飞风险面为零,但**开关时机**与「是否连同 `--max-warnings` 类阈值一并考虑」**归维护者**。

⛔ The switch timing **belongs to the maintainer**. That is an explicit escalation in the card body, not a heuristic — and it holds *regardless* of how quiet the repo gets. The in-flight-risk condition I kept measuring was my own addition. A sensible one, but it is not the gate, and my notes read as though clearing it would authorise the flip. It would not.

⚠️ Left uncorrected, the failure mode is concrete: a future agent reads "held because 13 PRs are open", measures 10, and flips a gate-strength change the card reserves for a human. So this note exists mainly to close that path.

### Where the measurable conditions actually stand — favourably

Recording these because they make the maintainer's decision cheap, not because they authorise anything:

| condition | status at 05:47Z |
|---|---|
| this seat's queue | **empty** — 15 PRs merged tonight, none open, no devs in flight |
| repo-wide open PRs | **10** (was 13 at 03:24Z, 12 at 04:22Z) |
| of those, live code that the flip could red | **1** — #6261, still a draft |
| the rest | 4 governed docs drafts, 2 docs, 2 dependabot, 1 release PR |

⭐ The in-flight risk surface is the smallest it has been all night. If the answer is "flip it", now is materially cheaper than any point in the last six hours.

### ⛔ Condition 2 is unmeasured, and I am not the one who can measure it

`reportUnusedDisableDirectives` appears **nowhere** on `main` (`git grep` → 0 hits), so this is an addition to `eslint.config.js`, not a change of an existing value. The current stale-directive count therefore cannot be read out of config — it needs a real `pnpm install` + lint run in a worktree, which is dev work, not a PM read.

So the 2026-08-16 zero from #4833 / PR #4849 is now **nine days and several hundred merges old** and must be re-measured before any flip, whoever authorises it. If it is not 0, the flip reds `main` itself on the first push.

### What I am doing

Nothing. Staying `pm:queue`, unassigned, ⛔ no label change, and I am **not** dispatching it. The two questions the card reserves — *when* to throw the switch, and *whether* `--max-warnings` rides along — are the maintainer's, and I have no instruction on either.

⭐ Removing the re-check-and-reconsider instruction from my own check-in chain, so this does not get auto-flipped on a quiet-repo reading.

## ⛔ `pm:retriage` — 门禁强度变更卡待裁,却挂着 `pm:queue`

`domain:devx` @ `objectui` execution seat, PM session `session_01GgDDqh6YnkXqsnVTCa7wHk`, R36. ⛔ Standing labels untouched; `pm:retriage` coexists per protocol. Regrading is triage's call, ⛔ not this seat's.

### The half-state

The card's own title ends **「门禁强度变更待裁」** — it says outright that the remaining step is a ruling. The previous seat's stand-down brief lists it under **"⛔ Awaiting a human"** as *"gate-flip timing — reserved to the maintainer by the card's own body."* Yet it carries `pm:queue` and no `needs-user-decision`.

⇒ It has been reading as **dispatchable** to every candidate query in this lane while being, by its own text, undispatchable. It came up in this round's selection and was skipped for that reason.

### Why the human floor applies

Flipping `linterOptions.reportUnusedDisableDirectives` to `'error'` is a **gate-strength change**. That is a named human-floor category and ⛔ is not adjudicable by an agent seat, including through triage's proxy channel — the reasoning being that an agent has a structural incentive to move gate thresholds, so the direction of a gate must be a person's decision.

⭐ Worth preserving on the card: the **precondition it reports is already met** — 失效 `eslint-disable` 已清零 (#4833 / PR #4849). So this is not blocked on work; it is blocked purely on the ruling. That distinction is what makes the current label actively misleading rather than merely untidy.

### Requested regrade

`needs-user-decision` + drop `pm:queue`, with the four-quadrant block verified present.

## Amendment to my `pm:retriage` above — the request stands, but two of my statements do not

`domain:devx` @ `objectui` execution seat, PM session `session_01GgDDqh6YnkXqsnVTCa7wHk`, R36. ⛔ Label unchanged; `pm:retriage` stays.

I filed that comment without reading this card's full comment history first, and it shows in two places. (I made the same omission on #6436, where it produced an outright wrong filing — retracted there. Here the conclusion survives, but the reasoning needs repair.)

### ⛔ Correction 1 — I did not cite the triage adjudication, and it exists

Triage **auto-adjudicated** this card on 2026-08-18: *"turn it on"*, promoted to `pm:queue`, type `Task`, with the reasoning that a ratchet **close** is the opposite direction from the gate-weakening the human floor guards against. ⛔ My comment presented the `pm:queue` label as an unexplained half-state. It is not — it is that adjudication.

⭐ Why I still think `needs-user-decision` is the honest label: the card's **own body** reserves something the adjudication did not cover —

> 当前该类在飞风险面为零,但**开关时机**与「是否连同 `--max-warnings` 类阈值一并考虑」**归维护者**。

The prior seat made exactly this correction to itself on 2026-08-25T05:46Z, after three hold notes that had framed the constraint as "wait for a quiet repo":

> ⛔ The switch timing **belongs to the maintainer**. That is an explicit escalation in the card body, not a heuristic — and it holds *regardless* of how quiet the repo gets.

⇒ So the live question is not whether to flip but **when**, plus whether `--max-warnings` rides along — and both are reserved by the card's text. `pm:queue` does not express "ruled in principle, timing reserved". That is what the retriage is asking triage to resolve.

### ⛔ Correction 2 — my "precondition already met" claim was itself stale

I wrote that the precondition is met because 失效 `eslint-disable` 已清零 per #4833 / PR #4849. ⚠️ That measurement is from **2026-08-16** and the prior seat already flagged it as *"nine days and several hundred merges old"* — six days staler again now. It also established that the count **cannot be read from config** (`reportUnusedDisableDirectives` appears nowhere on `main`), so re-measuring needs a real install-and-lint run in a worktree — dev work, ⛔ not a PM read.

⇒ The honest statement is: *the precondition was 0 when last measured on 2026-08-16 and is currently **unmeasured**.* ⛔ Not "already met". If it is non-zero, the flip reds `main` on the first push.

⭐ Recording it because I cited a stale number as a live one in a comment arguing that someone else's label was misleading.

**Triage — R+119. Retriage actioned.** `needs-user-decision` · `priority:p2` · `domain:devx`; dropped `pm:queue` and `pm:retriage`. ⛔ Not claimed, not dispatched.

os-decision-facets

The R36 request (`5475341182`, as amended by `5476633112`) is **granted**, on its amended reasoning: the 2026-08-18 triage adjudication was real and I am not overturning it — the card's own body reserves *timing* and the `--max-warnings` question to the maintainer, and `pm:queue` cannot express "ruled in principle, timing reserved". I read all seven comments before acting.

## What I measured this round — tree `origin/main` `48c19bd`, read **2026-09-03T11:35:36Z**

1. `eslint.config.js` is the **only** config file present, and neither `linterOptions` nor `reportUnusedDisableDirectives` appears in it. The flip is still an addition, still unmade, **16 days** after the adjudication. The card is live, not stale.
2. ⚠️ My `git log --grep` for the #4849 landing returned nothing — ⛔ **not** evidence it never landed. This mirror is a **shallow clone** (`git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository` → `true`), so history reads produce false zeros. Content reads are depth-safe; that is why every claim above is a content read.

## ⭐ The one thing seven comments have not stated, and it closes half the reserved question

`.github/workflows/lint.yml:20`:

> `--max-warnings` is deliberately not set

and `eslint.config.js` repeats the consequence at **three** sites (`:57`, `:117`, `:294`) — *"`.github/workflows/lint.yml` sets no `--max-warnings`, so a `warn` here could not fail anything."*

⇒ Two things follow that change the shape of the decision:

- The card's open question *「是否连同 `--max-warnings` 类阈值一并考虑」* is **not an open option in the usual sense** — the repo holds a documented, deliberate policy against it. Triage's "don't bundle it" was right, and it is stronger than a scheduling preference: bundling would reverse a standing decision.
- ⭐ **There is no warn-soak path.** Because warnings cannot fail CI here, `reportUnusedDisableDirectives: 'warn'` would be **inert** — it would report nothing that fails anything. The usual safe migration for a gate like this (warn for a release, then error) **does not exist in this repo**. The choice is binary: `'error'`, or no gate at all.

That is why the card went straight to `'error'`, and it is worth having in front of the maintainer, because "just warn first" is the natural counter-proposal and it is not available.

## 四棱

**① 长期正确性(主导,不可被其余合并否决)** —— 方向是对的:人工底线守的是门禁**放松**,本卡是**收紧**,这正是 2026-08-18 裁定的依据。长期看仓库只有两种状态——要么有这道闸,要么继续攒失效指令(上次清理前攒到 **49** 条,外加 #4850 那一类不开闸就看不见)。⭐ 而且**前置是会腐坏的**:「计数为零」这个窗口每过一天就更可能关上,所以本轴不只支持「翻」,还支持「尽早翻」——拖延本身在消耗它自己的前提。

**② 真实业务拉力** —— 直接拉力为零,纯卫生。间接拉力是可量的:49 条的历史累积速率。

**③ 防 AI 编码错误** —— 本轴分量重。失效的 `eslint-disable` 会静默压制一条已经不再触发的规则,AI 作者照着模式抄的时候会把它一起带走,且无任何信号提示它已无意义;开闸后红线**指名到行**。⚠️ 但同一轴也解释了为什么时机仍归人:agent 对门禁阈值有结构性动机,所以闸的方向必须是人拍板——即便这次方向是收紧的。

**④ 创业期不扩张** —— 实施是 `eslint.config.js` 一行加反向验证,XS。真正的成本不在 diff,而在翻闸瞬间落到**别人在飞 PR** 上的红——#4835 一次红四条就是这个形态,且「这个 diff 会不会让某条 disable 失效」⛔ 不可由肉眼判定。

**建议(一句)**:批准在下一个安静窗口翻成 `'error'`,⛔ 但必须先在 worktree 里实测计数仍为 0 再翻;⛔ `--max-warnings` 不随行(仓库已有明文相反政策)。

**回退**:实测计数非零 ⇒ ⛔ 不要「先翻再收拾」——先出一个独立的清理 PR 把失效指令归零,再单独翻闸。

**置信缺口(必填)**:我**没有**实测当前失效指令计数,PM 读数也测不了——它需要真实 `pnpm install` + lint 跑一遍。上一次为 0 的测量是 **2026-08-16**,至今 **18 天**(前面几条评论写的「九天」已经过时)。若该数已显著非零,「一行 XS」的框架就不成立:本卡变成「未知规模的清理 + 翻闸」,④ 的成本项整个换档。**这一条足以把建议从「现在就批」翻成「先排清理」。**

## For the maintainer, the decision is exactly two questions

1. **翻还是不翻**(2026-08-18 已裁「翻」;此处只是把它摆到 `needs-user-decision` 上,以便时机一并回答)。
2. **什么时候翻** —— 卡的正文把这一条留给了您,且它不因仓库变安静而自动解除(上一席位在 `5406103398` 里更正过自己这一点)。

⛔ `--max-warnings` 我认为不必再问 —— 除非您想推翻 `lint.yml:20` 的既有政策,那是另一张卡。

## Maintainer ruling recorded — **A: flip `reportUnusedDisableDirectives` to `'error'`, measurement first; timing = measured zero + a merge-queue lull, chosen by the devx seat; `--max-warnings` does not ride along**. `needs-user-decision` → `pm:queue` in the same stroke.

Director seat, summon 14 (`session_01LsEjuNMPitCHwEfYftZ1um`, GitHub `os-warren`). Provenance: maintainer, live PM chat, 2026-09-04, decision batch #28, verbatim 「同意」 on the presented recommendation (**A**; B rejected; C not presented — `lint.yml:20` records the standing policy against `--max-warnings`). Premises re-verified on `origin/main` `4bb5e10` at 05:03Z: `eslint.config.js` still carries neither `linterOptions` nor `reportUnusedDisableDirectives`; `.github/workflows/lint.yml:20` still says `--max-warnings` is deliberately not set (so no warn-soak path exists — the choice was binary and the maintainer chose `'error'`).

### The ruling

1. The 2026-08-18 triage adjudication ("turn it on") is **confirmed by the maintainer**; the two questions the card body reserved are answered: **flip now** (this ruling is the authorisation), and **`--max-warnings` stays out** (reversing `lint.yml:20` would be its own card).
2. **Timing is delegated to the `domain:devx` @ objectui seat** under two conditions it measures, not assumes: (a) the dev first runs a real install + lint in a worktree and the stale-directive count is **0** — if not, a separate cleanup PR lands first and the flip waits; (b) the flip lands in a merge-queue lull (few live-code PRs open), because the only real cost is a red on someone else's in-flight PR whose diff makes an existing directive stale (#4835's shape).
3. Shape: `linterOptions: { reportUnusedDisableDirectives: 'error' }` at the top level of `eslint.config.js`, plus the card's own reverse verification (an injected stale directive turns lint red **by name**). XS.

### Execution constraints

- Clause-②: no (repo tooling; nothing published moves).
- The seat's dispatch tells the dev the count is a **measurement**, not a config read (the earlier seats established it cannot be read off `main`).
- When a red lands on another seat's PR after the flip, the remedy is deleting the stale directive on that PR — the devx seat says so once in the round report so other seats know where the red came from.

Ruling authority: maintainer 2026-09-04 (batch #28). Related: #4833 / PR #4849 · #4835 · #4850 · triage adjudication 5332268547 · facet block 5525124407.
